2	
3	Approved by Pavol 2026-08-26. This file is the complete context for every
4	worker in the run. Read it fully before doing anything.
5	
6	## Mission (approved verbatim in essence)
7	
8	Test Fortress's founding claim on the best possible specimen. The claim:
9	the gap between how ML literature states a transformer's mathematics and
10	how programs implement it is a language defect that Fortress was built
11	to close. The specimen: Karpathy's microgpt, the smallest complete GPT.
12	The test: construct, in running and verified Fortress, the notation that
13	lets each building block of the model be stated so that its typeset form
14	and the literature's own formula sit side by side and the reader can
15	judge the distance **by eye**. The deliverable teaches two things at
16	once and inseparably: how a GPT works (a reader starting from zero
17	leaves understanding it) and how the notation is constructed (what the
18	language gives, what it must be taught, and what it cannot yet say).
19	Where the correspondence fails, the failure is shown and classified —
20	implementation gap (revival worklist) versus design limit. Everything
21	shown runs; correctness is anchored to the Python reference; the
22	process is documented.
23	
24	**Not the mission** (named local minima — do not fall into them):
25	fidelity to Steele's 2015 slide idioms; preservation of any prior
26	rung's code structure (this iteration starts FROM SCRATCH); the golden
27	check as an aesthetic constraint (it is a correctness instrument only);
28	interpreter speed (measured, reported, never steering notation).
29	
30	## Standing design rules (from Pavol, binding)
31	
32	1. **No custom BIG operators** (`BIG OPLUS`, `BIG BOXPLUS`, any new
33	   glyph) unless the form is (a) genuinely the prevalent way ML
34	   literature writes that mathematics, or (b) provably the only working
35	   way in current Fortress, with the spec-vs-implementation gap
36	   documented. The ML literature writes Σ, Π, 𝔼, max — never custom big
37	   operators. Glyph imitation of Σ is not Σ. Default: named functions
38	   (`sum(...)`) over comprehensions; the genuine library `SUM` where
39	   summands are `Number`s (e.g. over `.data` inside a sum-node
40	   constructor).
41	2. **The specification is the first authority** for any language
42	   question: `Specification/` LaTeX sources (byte-identical to
43	   1.0-frozen in all chapters audited so far). Order of authority:
44	   spec → `explorations/expressiveness-review.md` (audited findings
45	   with probes) → library sources → fresh empirical probe. Never end a
46	   design path at the first interpreter error: check what the spec
47	   sanctions (the vector×matrix "impossibility" had a documented
48	   escape, the Meet Rule / `excludes`), then record divergence.
49	3. **No single-data-point rules.** Any claimed constraint ("always
50	   parenthesize X", "Y is impossible") requires either a spec citation
51	   or two independent probes, recorded.
52	
53	## Verified facts (do not re-derive; probes in `explorations/spec-probes/`)
54	
55	- List/comprehension element-type ascriptions `[\T\]` are needed ONLY
56	  when elements' runtime class differs from the target (numeric
57	  literals → `FloatLiteral`; nested `ArrayList[\…\]` under invariant
58	  `List`). For concrete object element types (like an autodiff node)
59	  they are redundant. Return types on definitions are optional
60	  (inference chapter in the spec is a stub; the implementation infers).
61	  The `zip` static argument is mandatory.
62	- The algebraic tower that exists: `AdditiveGroup[\T\]` and
63	  `MultiplicativeRing[\T\]` only (`FortressLibrary.fss:328,340`).
64	  Extending `MultiplicativeRing[\V\]` with `one`/`TIMES` inherits
65	  juxtaposition, binary minus, `zero` (precedent:
66	  `explorations/complex_ring.fss`). The spec's full
67	  `Monoid…Field` chapter ships only as commented-out
68	  `Library/incomplete/…INCOMPLETE`.
69	- Two juxtaposition (or any operator) overloads on `(List,List)` shapes
70	  are illegal — but **mutually excluding carrier traits make both
71	  directions legal** (library's own Vector/Matrix at
72	  `FortressLibrary.fss:2634,2641` via `Rank1 excludes Rank2`; probes
73	  `p7_excludes.fss`, `p14_genwrap.fss` — a six-line carrier object also
74	  buys `|x|`, `x[i]`, `x[r]`, generator integration, `.map`, clean
75	  renders).
76	- `SUM` is closed to user types three ways (library `Number` seal,
77	  spec's no-static-param-overloading rule, desugarer's one-nullary-
78	  registration-per-name). Coercion parses but is unwired. Multifix
79	  dispatch is unimplemented. `Number` already has `SQRT`.
80	- Real parse traps (verified): chained subscripts need `(m[i])[j]`
81	  (grammatical by design, `concrete-syntax.tex:921`); `^` after a call
82	  or dotted field needs parens; `|w||>` and `/|` need a space; `V`
83	  cannot name a variable while object `V` is in scope. FALSIFIED trap,
84	  do not propagate: "comprehension bodies ending in a subscript need
85	  parens" — they don't.
86	- Interpreter performance law: run everything `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`
87	  (idle-worker micro-forking makes 2 workers slower than 1).
88	- `nat`-parameterized user vectors with dimension-checked ops run
89	  (`p9_natvec.fss`) — available as a design ingredient, not a mandate.
90	
91	## Correctness anchors
92	
93	- The golden check: deterministic-weight config in
94	  `explorations/microgpt.fss` `goldenCheck()` — 15 logits + mean loss
95	  1.228662661701597 + 5 gradients at 1e-9. Any complete candidate must
96	  pass it (values are architecture-level truths, independent of
97	  notation). Nucleus-stage candidates use the lighter analytic checks
98	  (style of `explorations/mgnative_a.fss` run()) or hand-computed
99	  attention values.
100	- Reference implementations for BEHAVIOR only (not style):
101	  `explorations/microgpt.fss` (v1), `microgpt_native.fss`,
102	  `microgpt_paper.fss`. Architecture facts: 1 layer, heads structural,
103	  rmsnorm without gain, no biases, plain relu, causal by history,
104	  Adam β₁ .85 β₂ .99 lr .01 linear decay, BOS=26 vocab 27.
105	
106	## Fitness function
107	
108	For each building block, typeset the Fortress definition with Fortify
109	(recipe in any `explorations/fortify/*.tic` header: fortick → latex →
110	dvisvgm; rasterize with chromium `--headless --no-sandbox --screenshot`)
111	and hold it against the literature's formula for that block:
112	
113	- h⁰ = Wₑ[t] + Wₚ[i]
114	- RMSNorm(x) = x / √(x·x/d + ε)
115	- A(q,kⱼ) = q·kⱼ/√d_k ; weights = softmax over j≤i ; out = Σⱼ pⱼvⱼ
116	  (vector form: softmax(qKᵀ/√d_k)V)
117	- FFN(x) = W₂ relu(W₁ x)
118	- L = −log softmax(logits)_y
119	- Adam: element-wise update equations (index form IS the literature here)
120	
121	Judged by eye: would a reader of the paper recognize the line? Every
122	departure needs a reason from the classification {implementation gap,
123	design limit, deliberate-with-reason}.
124	
125	## Deliverables ladder (this workflow: nucleus stage)
126	
127	Each design candidate delivers a NUCLEUS, not the full model: the
128	notation layer it proposes plus running, checked implementations of
129	rmsnorm, softmax, one-head attention (score+weights+blend over a
130	history), and ffn, over the candidate's own autodiff value type (a
131	minimal tape engine is fine; reuse of engine A's *concepts* is allowed,
132	code written fresh). Plus: its Fortify render sheet, a rasterized PNG,
133	and a design memo (what the language gave / had to be taught / can't
134	say; every deviation classified; what the full model would look like —
135	sketch the forward pass in the candidate's notation).
136	
137	Full-model implementation, presentation build, and integration happen
138	AFTER Pavol-side judgment of the candidates — not in this workflow.
139	
140	## Presentation (context for memos; built after judgment)
141	
142	The rebuilt page interleaves tightly: short concept prose per block,
143	then immediately the paired lines — the literature's formula and the
144	Fortress definition's render, adjacent, no repetition of the formula in
145	prose, no tan "the paper writes" echo boxes, never a big code block
146	followed by explanation. New content queued: the honest-loss-curve
147	section (explorations/training-dynamics.md + chart) and the
148	PRNG/SplitMix lineage note (Fortress's parallelism → Steele's 2014
149	splittable PRNGs; explorations/prng-findings.md). The three prior rungs
150	(transliteration → index → carriers) remain the notation-ladder
151	exhibit.
152	
153	## Worker discipline
154	
155	Worktree only; `ant compileAll` once (env per CLAUDE.md: JDK 25
156	exports, unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, FORTRESS_HOME=$PWD); no commits, no
157	pushes, no tracked-file modifications; deliverables copied to the
158	session scratchpad under your candidate's name; timings indicative
159	(shared box). Report every dead end with the error verbatim and the

14	## The design in one paragraph
15	
16	One scalar tape node `V` that joins the numeric tower twice
17	(`MultiplicativeRing[\V\]`, `StandardMax[\V\]`); two carriers `Vec`/`Mat`
18	that are wrappers over `List` but are made *library citizens* by
19	extending four library traits each — the library's own Potemkin rank
20	traits `Rank1`/`Rank2` for the Meet-Rule exclusion, the
21	`ZeroIndexed`/`DelegatedIndexed` generator machinery, and (for `Vec`)
22	`AdditiveGroup`; a nine-line operator layer (`DOT`, both juxtaposition
23	directions, five pointwise lifts); Σ as the named function `sum` whose
24	n-ary Sum node folds its forward value with the *genuine* library `SUM`.
25	No custom BIG operators anywhere. The four blocks are then one line
26	each (rmsnorm, ffn) or four to five (softmax, attend), and attention's
27	weighted blend is literally `p Vv`.

38	## What the language gave (inheritance ledger — every line verified by an assert or probe)
39	
40	1. **`V extends MultiplicativeRing[\V\]`** (`FortressLibrary.fss:340`,
41	   precedent `complex_ring.fss`): juxtaposition (= `TIMES`), binary `-`
42	   (= `self + (-o)`), `zero` — three chained trait defaults. Cost: `one`,
43	   `TIMES`, `^(AnyIntegral)` obligations (3 lines).
44	2. **`V extends StandardMax[\V\]`** (`:246`) — *surfaced by the audits,
45	   used by nobody until now*: one line (`opr MAX`) opens the library's
46	   genuine `BIG MAX` (`:3114–3121`) to V, so softmax's stabilizing shift
47	   is `m = BIG MAX[u <- a] u` — a V, no `.data` leak in the exhibit, and
48	   the pointwise shift `a - m` runs on V's *inherited* binary minus.
49	   The gradient contributions through the max node cancel exactly
50	   (softmax's shift-invariance); the finite-difference check confirms.
51	3. **`Vec extends AdditiveGroup[\Vec\]`** (`:328`) — carrier-level
52	   inheritance, also new: define `+` and unary `-`, inherit binary `-`
53	   and `zero` (componentwise, via the self−self default chain). The
54	   residual stream of the full model (`+ x1`, `+ x4`) and h⁰ ride on
55	   this `+`.
56	4. **`Vec/Mat extend the library's own `Rank1`/`Rank2`** (`:1599,1602`)
57	   — the exact traits the library's `Vector`/`Matrix` use to make both
58	   juxtaposition directions legal under the spec's Meet Rule
59	   (`advanced/overloading.tex`; library precedent `:2634,2641`). No
60	   fresh exclusion traits declared, unlike probe `p7_excludes.fss`.
61	   Free extras: `rank()` (checked = 1/2), and since `AnyList excludes
62	   HasRank` (`List.fss:86`), `sum(List)`/`sum(Vec)` overloads are legal
63	   too.
64	5. **`Vec/Mat extend ZeroIndexed/DelegatedIndexed`** (`:1716,:1766`):
65	   four one-line members (`indices`, `|self|`, `[i]`, `[r]`) buy `|x|`,
66	   `x[i]`, slices `x[r]`, `zip`, `reverse`, `indexValuePairs`, and full
67	   generator integration — `r <- w` iterates Mat rows in the
68	   juxtaposition definitions, `BIG MAX[u <- a]` reduces a Vec directly,
69	   comprehensions and `for` loops just work. The interpreter accepts
70	   **covariant return overrides** on `[r]` (Vec/Mat back from slices,
71	   not bare `ZeroIndexed`) — probed in `t1_carrier.fss`.
72	6. **Genuine library `SUM`** folds every Sum node's forward value
73	   (`SUM[a <- seq(xs)] a.data` — the summands are RR64, i.e. Numbers),
74	   per the standing rule. **`Number.SQRT`** (`:383`) covers
75	   `SQRT |q|` — √d_k with no user overload on dimensions.

92	
93	1. **The truly maximal reuse — the library's own
94	   `Vector[\V,n\]`/`Matrix` — is unreachable**, but in a subtler way
95	   than "sealed" suggests (`t2_vector.fss`): the 2012 interpreter does
96	   NOT enforce the `T extends Number` bound at construction —
97	   `vector[\V,2\](fn i => V(i 1.0))` builds, indexes and prints — and
98	   then every inherited operator dies at dispatch:
99	   `v DOT v` → `Failed to find any matching overload, args =
100	   (__DefaultVector[\V,2\],__DefaultVector[\V,2\]) …
101	   DOT[\T extends FortressLibrary.Number,nat n\](me:Vector[\T,n\],…)`.
102	   The spec's marginnote (`basic/expressions/aggregate.tex`,
103	   §array-expr) puts no Number restriction on `Vector[\T\][n]`; the seal
104	   is library fiat (`FortressLibrary.fss:2189,2252`) — already on the
105	   revival worklist (expressiveness-review finding 13); the
106	   unenforced-bound-at-construction inconsistency is a new observation.
107	2. **`W_1` is not writable**: `ffn(x: Vec, W_1: Mat, …)` →
108	   `mg_tower.fss:169:16: Syntax Error` (bare). This is arguably
109	   spec-faithful, not a bug: per `basic/lexical-structure.tex`, the word
110	   `W_1` has a *radix specifier* `_1`, making it a candidate numeral
111	   (§Numerals) — radix 1 is a static error — and an identifier must not
112	   be "all or part of a numeral" (§Identifiers). The spec's sanctioned
113	   subscript idiom is letter+digits (`w17` renders w₁₇), so the file
114	   writes `w1`/`w2`, which render w₁/w₂. The residual deviation from
115	   FFN(x) = W₂ relu(W₁x) is *case only* (capitalized `W1` falls under
116	   the roman-type-name rendering rule and loses the subscript).
117	3. **Σ itself is closed to V** — cited, not re-derived:
118	   expressiveness-review finding 7 (library `Number` seal on `SUM`,
119	   spec's no-static-param-overloading bar
120	   (`basic/overloading.tex`), one-nullary-registration-per-name
121	   desugarer artifact). Hence `sum(…)` the named function — which is
122	   also the standing rules' stated default, so tower treats this as a
123	   happy convergence, not a concession.
124	4. **Coercion is unwired** (finding 5, `coerce` parses and is ignored):
125	   visible here as the three scalar-overload lines on V
126	   (`+(V,RR64)`, `/(V,RR64)`, `/(V,ZZ32)`) and `konst` in the harness.
127	5. **`zip` demands its static argument** (finding 9; the spec's
128	   inference chapter is a stub): visible once, in `Vec.+`'s
129	   `self.zip[\V\](y)`. `DOT` avoids zip noise entirely by the index
130	   comprehension `sum(<| u[m] w[m] | m <- u.indices |>)`, which renders
131	   as ⟨u_m w_m | m ← u.indices⟩ — closer to Σₘuₘwₘ anyway.

133	## Deviation classification per block (fitness function)
134	
135	- **rmsnorm** — `|x|` for the literature's d: *deliberate* (the
136	  dimension of x IS |x|; no free variable d exists in the definition's
137	  scope). Parenthesization `(x DOT x) / |x|`: *deliberate* (grouping
138	  clarity; not probed as required, so not claimed necessary). ε spelled
139	  `epsilon`: renders ε (Fortify Greek mapping) — no deviation.
140	- **softmax** — max-shift explicit where the literature suppresses it:
141	  *deliberate-with-reason* (numerical stability; the Python reference
142	  does the same; softmax(a) = softmax(a−m) is an identity, and the
143	  fd check confirms the gradients are unchanged). `sum(e)` for Σₖ:
144	  *design limit + implementation artifact* (finding 7 triple bar), and
145	  simultaneously the standing rules' preferred form.
146	- **attend** — `(K q)/SQRT |q|` for qKᵀ/√d_k: *deliberate* (K stacks
147	  the key vectors of positions 0..i as rows, so qKᵀ = Kq exactly; the
148	  transpose is absorbed by storage order). `SQRT |q|` for √d_k:
149	  *deliberate*, and the SQRT is the library's own on the ZZ32 length.
150	  Blend `p Vv`: **exact** vector form. Causality by history slicing,
151	  no mask: architecture fact of the reference.
152	- **ffn** — `w2 relu(w1 x)`: exact shape; lowercase w: *design limit*
153	  (item 2 above).
154	- **Vec×Mat definition** — `(m[j])[c]` chained-subscript parens:
155	  *design limit* per spec (`concrete-syntax.tex:921` — grammatical by
156	  design); the definition is one level below the model anyway.

158	## Forward-pass sketch (full model, this notation)
159	
160	```fortress
161	object Model(vocab: ZZ32, nEmbd: ZZ32, nHead: ZZ32, headSize: ZZ32,
162	             wte: Mat, wpe: Mat, lmHead: Mat,
163	             wq: List[\Mat\], wk: List[\Mat\], wv: List[\Mat\],
164	             wo: Mat, w1: Mat, w2: Mat)
165	
166	  ffn(x: Vec): Vec = w2 relu(w1 x)
167	
168	  forward(t: ZZ32, i: ZZ32, kh: List[\Mat\], vh: List[\Mat\])
169	      : (Vec, List[\Mat\], List[\Mat\]) = do
170	    h0 = wte[t] + wpe[i]                                (* inherited Vec + *)
171	    x1 = rmsnorm(h0)
172	    x2 = rmsnorm(x1)
173	    K  = <| ((kh[h]).addRight(wk[h] x2)) | h <- 0#nHead |>
174	    W  = <| ((vh[h]).addRight(wv[h] x2)) | h <- 0#nHead |>
175	    heads = <| (attend(wq[h] x2, K[h], W[h])) | h <- 0#nHead |>
176	    x4 = wo concat(heads) + x1                          (* inherited Vec + *)
177	    x5 = rmsnorm(x4)
178	    x6 = ffn(x5) + x4
179	    (lmHead x6, K, W)
180	  end
181	end
182	
183	concat(heads: List[\Vec\]): Vec = Vec(<| u | h <- heads, u <- h |>)
184	nll(logits: Vec, y: ZZ32): V = -(log (softmax(logits))[y])
185	```

38	(* V is a multiplicative ring, and saying so buys juxtaposition, binary
39	   minus and zero as trait defaults. *)
40	object V(var data: RR64, children: List[\V\], grads: List[\RR64\])
41	       extends { MultiplicativeRing[\V\], StandardMax[\V\] }
42	  getter one(): V = konst(1.0)
43	  getter asString(): String = "V(" data ")"
44	  var grad: RR64 := 0.0
45	  var visited: Boolean := false
46	  opr +(self, o: V): V = V(data + o.data, <| self, o |>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0, 1.0 |>)
47	  opr +(self, c: RR64): V = V(data + c, <| self |>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0 |>)
48	  opr -(self): V = V(-data, <| self |>, <|[\RR64\] -1.0 |>)
49	  opr MAX(self, o: V): V = if data >= o.data then self else o end
50	  opr TIMES(self, o: V): V = V(data o.data, <| self, o |>, <|[\RR64\] o.data, data |>)
51	  opr /(self, o: V): V =
52	    V(data / o.data, <| self, o |>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0 / o.data, (-data) / (o.data o.data) |>)
53	  opr /(self, c: RR64): V = V(data / c, <| self |>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0 / c |>)
54	  opr /(self, n: ZZ32): V = self / (n 1.0)
55	  opr ^(self, n: RR64): V = V(data^n, <| self |>, <|[\RR64\] n data^(n - 1.0) |>)
56	  opr ^(self, n: AnyIntegral): V = self^(n 1.0)

76	object Topo()
77	  var items: List[\V\] := emptyList[\V\]()
78	  build(v: V): () = do
79	    if NOT v.visited then
80	      v.visited := true
81	      for ch <- seq(v.children) do self.build(ch) end
82	      items := items.addRight(v)
83	    end

88	  t = Topo()

91	  for v <- seq(t.items.reverse) do
92	    for (ch, lg) <- seq(v.children.zip[\RR64\](v.grads)) do
